CHORD RFI-monitor spectrum & H-line visibility

Interactive assessment of hydrogen recombination line visibility against measured RFI.

Instructions

Pick a line from the Zoom to line dropdown to jump to a given H nα line, or drag a box on either panel to zoom into a region, double click to reset zoom. The two panels share the frequency axis, and hovering reports the frequency, value and clean/RFI status.

Description

Top panel — 10 power samples from the RFI monitor for each frequency bin, resampled to 50 km/s resolution.

Bottom panel — the calibrated spectral kurtosis (SK) per channel, green where the channel is clean and red where it is flagged as RFI. Dashed verticals mark the H nα lines.

Methods

Segments

The monitor records 11 usable time segments between calibration cycles. All statistics are computed independently per segment and combined at the end.

Spectral kurtosis

Within a segment, each channel accumulates the power sums \(S_1=\sum P\) and \(S_2=\sum P^2\) over its \(M\) time integrations. The generalised SK estimator is

$$\widehat{SK} = \frac{Nd\,M + 1}{M-1}\left(\frac{M\,S_2}{S_1^2} - 1\right),$$

where \(Nd\) is the calibrated shape parameter. RFI-free data sits at \(\widehat{SK}\approx 1\).

Clean / RFI thresholds

A channel is flagged as RFI when its SK falls outside the central 0.1%–99.9% range of an RFI-free SK distribution, simulated from \(\mathrm{Gamma}(Nd,1)\) draws:

$$SK_{0.1\%} < \widehat{SK} < SK_{99.9\%}, \qquad [0.791,\ 1.242].$$

Segments are combined by majority vote: a channel is clean when more than 50% of segments agree, leaving 76.3% of channels clean.

Per-line visibility score

Each H nα line is scored by the Gaussian-weighted fraction of clean bins in a 100 km/s window (\(\sigma = f_0\,v/c\)):

$$\mathrm{score}(f_0) = \frac{\sum_i w_i\,\mathrm{clean}_i}{\sum_i w_i}, \quad w_i = e^{-\tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{f_i - f_0}{\sigma}\right)^2}.$$

A line is usable when its score \(\ge 0.99\): 79 / 116 lines qualify.
